trends.trend: Home/auto insurance affordability and availability; residual markets and regulated rates
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Whether a household can buy home cover at all, and from whom: State Farm General +17% in California, FAIR Plan at 698,307 policies and USD 773bn exposure, Florida Citizens down to 278,246 policies at mid-2026 after mass takeouts, with rate cuts for most policyholders, national carriers not writing new homeowners in Florida, auto premiums now falling. Mortgages, home values and migration follow.

trends.trend: Insurers pricing or excluding AI and cyber risk
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: From January 2026 standard liability forms can exclude anything 'arising out of generative artificial intelligence', and D&O carriers have absolute AI exclusions, while a small affirmative market (USD 15-25m limits) forms. Whether a business deploying AI agents is insured, and at what price, determines how fast AI is adopted and who pays when it fails; cyber rates are still falling.

trends.trend: Wildfire and climate liability shifting to utilities, ratepayers and public backstops
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Mega-fire losses are moving off insurers' books onto utility customers and state funds: Eaton Fire litigation (38,000 plaintiffs, bellwether trials in 2027), the California Wildfire Fund, customer-funded self-insurance collected through electric rates, NFIP on serial short-term extensions, TWIA cutting required funding from 1-in-100 to 1-in-50. Shows up in power bills, surcharges and assessments.

trends.trend: Carbon prices and the warming trajectory (policy and physical baseline)
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: EU allowances trade around EUR 85/t with ETS2 on heating and road fuel due in 2028; California allowances clear near USD 32; pledges imply ~2.6C. A strong 2026-27 El Nino has markets pricing 2026 as the hottest year on record at ~92%. These set fuel, heating and food prices and the physical baseline the insurers above are pricing.
